investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Blocked
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No new agents can be provisioned in the production environment, causing the entire remote-agents feature eval to fail at the creation step before any VM readiness or runtime assertions can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard agent quota of 100. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T21:04:00Z), that quota was already at or above its limit, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 Conflict with the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three sibling checks depend on successfully creating an agent via the same endpoint, all fail with the identical error message. The eval never reaches VM provisioning or runtime state assertions.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} — observed in failedCheck.message

All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is at the shared agent-creation step, not in downstream VM or runtime logic.
Evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was created and no downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) were ever evaluated.
Latency for all three calls is low (1510 ms, 1064 ms, 995 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.
The nested swarm error code is 'conflict' with message 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm layer itself enforces the cap and returned it synchronously.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm org has reached its hard agent quota of 100 and existing agents have not been cleaned up, leaving no room for the eval's probe agent to be created.
[Likely] A previous eval run or automated process created agents that were not deleted after use, causing quota to accumulate over time until the limit was hit.
[Possible] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown after each run, so each failed or successful run leaks an agent slot, eventually exhausting the quota.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or was recently lowered for the production org, causing previously-passing runs to now fail.
[Less likely] A separate workload (user traffic, another automation) consumed the remaining quota slots concurrently with the eval run, causing a race condition.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle assertions, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 and is returning a conflict error when the eval attempts to create a new agent via POST /api/agents. Because all three sibling checks share the same agent-creation step as their prerequisite, a single quota exhaustion at the swarm layer causes a cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature check suite. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} — present identically in all three check messages.

All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the exact same 409 error message, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation call, not at downstream state or runtime polling.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state in evidence, but evidence is empty ({}) for all three checks — consistent with the agent never being created.
Latencies for all three checks are well under the 5000 ms warning threshold (1510 ms, 1064 ms, 995 ms), ruling out a timeout or latency-related failure; the error is a hard rejection.
The swarm error message explicitly states the limit: "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the quota ceiling has been reached in the target environment.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Eval environment agent quota is exhausted: a prior eval run (or multiple runs) created agents that were not cleaned up, accumulating to the 100-agent limit and blocking new provisioning.
[Likely] Eval teardown/cleanup logic is not reliably deleting agents after each run, causing quota to grow monotonically across runs until the hard limit is hit.

[Possible] The eval harness is running in the production environment (environment: production is set in the check config) and is sharing the quota with real workloads or other automated processes, accelerating quota exhaustion.

[Less likely] The swarm quota limit of 100 is too low for the combined load of eval runs plus any other agent consumers in this environment, requiring a quota increase rather than (or in addition to) a cleanup fix.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting agents toward the quota (e.g., counting soft-deleted or terminated agents as active).

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle assertions, so no expected-output evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 for the target org/environment. At the time the eval ran (2026-06-14T21:04:02–04Z), that quota was already at or above its limit, causing every POST /api/agents call to return 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval suite depends on successfully creating a new agent as its first step, all downstream checks (state, runtime, chat readiness) cascade-fail before any assertions can be evaluated. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a production user-traffic outage.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned identical 409 error bodies: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the org-level or environment-level agent cap has been reached.

remote-agent-create failed first (endedAt 21:04:02.439Z), followed by remote-agent-state (21:04:03.503Z) and remote-agent-runtime (21:04:04.498Z), consistent with a sequential eval pipeline where each step depends on agent creation.
No evidence fields were populated in any check's evidence object, confirming zero successful agent provisioning occurred.

Latencies for all three calls (995 ms, 1064 ms, 1510 ms) are well below the warningLatencyMs (20000 ms) and outageLatencyMs (60000 ms) thresholds, ruling out a timeout or performance degradation as the cause — the failure is a hard quota rejection, not slowness.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Eval agents from previous runs were not cleaned up, causing accumulated agents to exhaust the 100-agent quota. Each eval run creates an agent but a teardown/delete step is missing or failing silently.
[Likely] The eval org/project used in the production environment shares its agent quota with real workloads or other automated processes, and the combined count has hit 100.
[Possible] A prior eval run crashed mid-execution after creating agents but before deleting them, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Less likely] The swarm backend's quota enforcement was recently lowered or a quota reset that was expected to run did not execute, shrinking available headroom.
[Less likely] A separate automated process (e.g., a load test, a staging promotion, or a CI pipeline) is creating agents in the same org and competing for quota.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the target URL.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the media generation pipeline attempted to open a session, causing the stream to abort at session-open time. The required evidence keys `frameTypes` (containing `generation_completed`) and `imageUrlPresent` were never populated because no generation work was performed. This is an eval-environment infrastructure failure — the harness endpoint resolved by `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL` is either absent, mis-routed, or version-incompatible — not a logic failure in the generation pipeline itself.
proof: Frame 1 — `generation_start` with `mode: image` was emitted, confirming the stream was initiated correctly by the client.

Frame 2 — `generation_error` event carries `code: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
Frame 3 — A bare `message` event with null data and empty raw payload was emitted, indicating the stream terminated abnormally with no further content.
Required evidence keys `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are both absent from the collected evidence, consistent with the stream never reaching a generation phase.
Eval latency was 2017 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the failure was a fast, hard error at session-open, not a timeout or slow generation.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The harness pod or process is not running at the URL configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL in the eval environment, causing every session-open request to 404.

[Likely] The harness was deployed but the route or path segment for the session-open endpoint changed in a newer harness version, making the URL the client constructs invalid (version incompatibility).
[Possible] The harness is running but behind a proxy or ingress that is misconfigured, dropping or mis-routing requests to the session-open path and returning 404.
[Possible] The environment variable LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is unset, empty, or points to a stale/decommissioned host, so the 404 comes from a default or fallback handler.
[Less likely] A recent deployment rolled back or replaced the harness image with an older version that does not expose the expected session-open endpoint.

reproductionSteps.label: Confirm the harness URL configuration in the eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Verify that exactly one of these is set and resolves to the intended harness host. An empty or wrong value will reproduce the 404.

reproductionSteps.label: Probe the harness session-open endpoint directly
reproductionSteps.details: A 404 response here confirms the harness is unreachable or the path is wrong. A connection-refused or DNS error points to the host being absent entirely.

reproductionSteps.label: Check harness process / pod health in the eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect running processes or container/pod status for the agent runtime harness. Confirm it is in a Running/healthy state and listening on the expected port.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the image-generation-stream eval after confirming harness reachability
reproductionSteps.details: Once the harness URL is corrected and the harness is confirmed reachable, re-trigger the eval to verify that `generation_completed` appears in frameTypes and `imageUrlPresent` equals true.

affectedAreas.reason: The harness may not be deployed, may have been replaced with an incompatible version, or may be behind a misconfigured proxy — all of which manifest as a 404 at session-open time.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the eval environment and confirm LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is set to the correct, reachable harness base URL before the next eval run.
Verify the harness process/container is running and healthy in the target environment; check deployment logs for crash-loops, failed rollouts, or version mismatches.
Curl the session-open endpoint directly from the eval runner host to isolate whether the 404 is a DNS/routing issue, a missing route, or a version-incompatible API path.
If a harness version upgrade was recently deployed, confirm the session-open endpoint path has not changed and that the eval client is using the matching API contract.

Add a pre-flight connectivity check to the eval harness that validates harness reachability and version compatibility before attempting to open a generation session, so failures surface as a clearer 'harness not ready' signal rather than a mid-stream error.

Scope the incident to the eval environment only — no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; do not escalate as a production outage without additional signals.
followUpEvals: Harness reachability pre-check eval: assert that a lightweight health/ping endpoint on the agent runtime harness returns 200 before any generation eval is attempted.
Harness version compatibility eval: assert that the harness-reported API version matches the version expected by the eval client, catching incompatible deployments before session-open.
Environment variable presence eval: assert that LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is non-empty and resolves to a reachable host at eval startup.
Session-open latency eval: assert that session-open completes within a defined threshold (e.g., 5000 ms) to catch slow or partially-broken harness deployments that do not immediately 404.

Full stream completion eval (regression): once the harness is restored, assert the full happy-path — `generation_start` → one or more progress frames → `generation_completed` in frameTypes → `imageUrlPresent` equals true — to confirm end-to-end generation is functional.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the target URL.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the media generation pipeline attempted to open a session, causing the stream to abort at session-open time. The required evidence keys `frameTypes` (containing `generation_completed`) and `imageUrlPresent` were never populated because no generation work was performed. This is an eval-environment infrastructure failure — the harness endpoint resolved by `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL` is either absent, mis-routed, or version-incompatible — not a logic failure in the generation pipeline itself.
proof: Frame 1 — `generation_start` with `mode: image` was emitted, confirming the stream was initiated correctly by the client.

Frame 2 — `generation_error` event carries `code: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
Frame 3 — A bare `message` event with null data and empty raw payload was emitted, indicating the stream terminated abnormally with no further content.
Required evidence keys `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are both absent from the collected evidence, consistent with the stream never reaching a generation phase.
Eval latency was 2017 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the failure was a fast, hard error at session-open, not a timeout or slow generation.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The harness pod or process is not running at the URL configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL in the eval environment, causing every session-open request to 404.

[Likely] The harness was deployed but the route or path segment for the session-open endpoint changed in a newer harness version, making the URL the client constructs invalid (version incompatibility).
[Possible] The harness is running but behind a proxy or ingress that is misconfigured, dropping or mis-routing requests to the session-open path and returning 404.
[Possible] The environment variable LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is unset, empty, or points to a stale/decommissioned host, so the 404 comes from a default or fallback handler.
[Less likely] A recent deployment rolled back or replaced the harness image with an older version that does not expose the expected session-open endpoint.

reproductionSteps.label: Confirm the harness URL configuration in the eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Verify that exactly one of these is set and resolves to the intended harness host. An empty or wrong value will reproduce the 404.

reproductionSteps.label: Probe the harness session-open endpoint directly
reproductionSteps.details: A 404 response here confirms the harness is unreachable or the path is wrong. A connection-refused or DNS error points to the host being absent entirely.

reproductionSteps.label: Check harness process / pod health in the eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect running processes or container/pod status for the agent runtime harness. Confirm it is in a Running/healthy state and listening on the expected port.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the image-generation-stream eval after confirming harness reachability
reproductionSteps.details: Once the harness URL is corrected and the harness is confirmed reachable, re-trigger the eval to verify that `generation_completed` appears in frameTypes and `imageUrlPresent` equals true.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Blocked
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No new agents can be provisioned in the production environment, causing the entire remote-agents feature eval to fail at the creation step before any VM readiness or runtime assertions can be evaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard agent quota of 100. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T21:04:00Z), that quota was already at or above its limit, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 Conflict with the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three sibling checks depend on successfully creating an agent via the same endpoint, all fail with the identical error message. The eval never reaches VM provisioning or runtime state assertions.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} — observed in failedCheck.message

All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is at the shared agent-creation step, not in downstream VM or runtime logic.
Evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was created and no downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) were ever evaluated.
Latency for all three calls is low (1510 ms, 1064 ms, 995 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.
The nested swarm error code is 'conflict' with message 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm layer itself enforces the cap and returned it synchronously.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm org has reached its hard agent quota of 100 and existing agents have not been cleaned up, leaving no room for the eval's probe agent to be created.
[Likely] A previous eval run or automated process created agents that were not deleted after use, causing quota to accumulate over time until the limit was hit.
[Possible] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown after each run, so each failed or successful run leaks an agent slot, eventually exhausting the quota.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or was recently lowered for the production org, causing previously-passing runs to now fail.
[Less likely] A separate workload (user traffic, another automation) consumed the remaining quota slots concurrently with the eval run, causing a race condition.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt to create a new remote agent via the agents API in production
reproductionSteps.details: Send a valid agent creation payload to the production endpoint. Expect HTTP 409 with 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if quota is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Query current agent count for the production org
reproductionSteps.details: Use the agents list or admin API to count active agents in the production org and confirm whether the count is at or near 100.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect agent lifecycle — check for leaked/orphaned agents
reproductionSteps.details: List all agents in the production org and identify any that are in a terminal or idle state but have not been deleted, particularly those created by eval or automation runs.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt agent deletion of a known orphaned agent, then retry creation
reproductionSteps.details: Delete one or more orphaned agents and immediately retry POST /api/agents to confirm the quota error resolves and creation succeeds.

reproductionSteps.label: Review eval harness teardown logic
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the eval runner for remote-agent-create to confirm whether it issues a DELETE for the probe agent after each run, or whether agents are left behind.

investigations.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle assertions, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 and is returning a conflict error when the eval attempts to create a new agent via POST /api/agents. Because all three sibling checks share the same agent-creation step as their prerequisite, a single quota exhaustion at the swarm layer causes a cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature check suite. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} — present identically in all three check messages.

All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the exact same 409 error message, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation call, not at downstream state or runtime polling.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state in evidence, but evidence is empty ({}) for all three checks — consistent with the agent never being created.
Latencies for all three checks are well under the 5000 ms warning threshold (1510 ms, 1064 ms, 995 ms), ruling out a timeout or latency-related failure; the error is a hard rejection.
The swarm error message explicitly states the limit: "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the quota ceiling has been reached in the target environment.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Eval environment agent quota is exhausted: a prior eval run (or multiple runs) created agents that were not cleaned up, accumulating to the 100-agent limit and blocking new provisioning.
[Likely] Eval teardown/cleanup logic is not reliably deleting agents after each run, causing quota to grow monotonically across runs until the hard limit is hit.

[Possible] The eval harness is running in the production environment (environment: production is set in the check config) and is sharing the quota with real workloads or other automated processes, accelerating quota exhaustion.

[Less likely] The swarm quota limit of 100 is too low for the combined load of eval runs plus any other agent consumers in this environment, requiring a quota increase rather than (or in addition to) a cleanup fix.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting agents toward the quota (e.g., counting soft-deleted or terminated agents as active).

investigations.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle assertions, so no expected-output evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 for the target org/environment. At the time the eval ran (2026-06-14T21:04:02–04Z), that quota was already at or above its limit, causing every POST /api/agents call to return 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval suite depends on successfully creating a new agent as its first step, all downstream checks (state, runtime, chat readiness) cascade-fail before any assertions can be evaluated. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a production user-traffic outage.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned identical 409 error bodies: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the org-level or environment-level agent cap has been reached.

remote-agent-create failed first (endedAt 21:04:02.439Z), followed by remote-agent-state (21:04:03.503Z) and remote-agent-runtime (21:04:04.498Z), consistent with a sequential eval pipeline where each step depends on agent creation.
No evidence fields were populated in any check's evidence object, confirming zero successful agent provisioning occurred.

Latencies for all three calls (995 ms, 1064 ms, 1510 ms) are well below the warningLatencyMs (20000 ms) and outageLatencyMs (60000 ms) thresholds, ruling out a timeout or performance degradation as the cause — the failure is a hard quota rejection, not slowness.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Eval agents from previous runs were not cleaned up, causing accumulated agents to exhaust the 100-agent quota. Each eval run creates an agent but a teardown/delete step is missing or failing silently.
[Likely] The eval org/project used in the production environment shares its agent quota with real workloads or other automated processes, and the combined count has hit 100.
[Possible] A prior eval run crashed mid-execution after creating agents but before deleting them, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Less likely] The swarm backend's quota enforcement was recently lowered or a quota reset that was expected to run did not execute, shrinking available headroom.
[Less likely] A separate automated process (e.g., a load test, a staging promotion, or a CI pipeline) is creating agents in the same org and competing for quota.
